cards.text: The LORD gives Moses, Israel's leader, a message to pass on to the Israelites. It opens with who's talking: "I am the LORD your God."

Then God names two lands whose practices Israel must NOT follow: the one they used to live in, and the one He's bringing them into. That's like moving to a new house and hearing, "Don't bring the old neighborhood's habits with you, and DON'T pick up the new neighborhood's either."

cards.question: God says don't follow the practices of the land Israel used to live in, or of the land He's bringing them into. Which two lands are they?
So how DOES Israel live? Not Egypt's way and not Canaan's way. God tells them to work out a way of their own somewhere in between.
God tells Israel to keep His statutes and His judgments. What reason does He give?

answers.text: The man who does them will live by them
The nations around them will honor them
Their enemies will run away from them

cards.text: Then comes a long list of practices God forbids, starting with this: "None of you are to approach any close relative to have sexual relations." He walks through the family, from mother and sister to aunt and daughter-in-law, and often gives the reason, like it would dishonor a father or shame the family. He also forbids sexual relations with a neighbor's wife and with any animal, and says a man must not lie with a man as with a woman, which He calls an abomination. And no one may give any of their children to be sacrificed to Molech, a god the Ammonites worshiped (1 Kings 11:7).
God's still giving Moses His message for Israel. He says, "Do not defile yourselves by any of these practices," and then He tells them why.

cards.question: God says the ___ He is driving out before Israel have defiled themselves by all these things.
God says even the land has become defiled, and He is punishing it for its sin. What will the land do to its inhabitants?

cards.text: Then God says it plainly: Israel is to keep His statutes and ordinances and not commit any of these abominations.

cards.question: God says the foreigner who lives among Israel must not commit any of these abominations either.

cards.text: Then God reminds them: the men who were in the land before them committed all these abominations, and the land became defiled.

cards.question: Since God is bringing Israel into the land, He says it will never vomit them out, no matter what they do there.
What does God say must happen to anyone who commits any of these abominations?

answers.text: He must be cut off from his people
He must offer a lamb at the altar
He must stay outside the camp a week

cards.text: God closes by telling Israel to keep His charge and stay away from the customs practiced before them, and He ends right where He began: "I am the LORD your God." But God's not done teaching His people what it looks like to be His, friend, so keep that apron on.
